notes: Rebuilt JACK IN from endpoint lines into a branching network topology
Added synthetic non-interactive gateway, relay, subnet, edge, and port nodes so sparse scenes still read as a live network
Added backbone, branch, mesh, endpoint, shadow, and selected-route link classes
Added animated packet traffic across the network and stronger yellow traffic on the selected target route
Selected targets now highlight the full operator-to-relay-to-endpoint route instead of only the final connection
Operator is now a network hub with rotating rings, radial uplink spokes, and pulsing port markers
Selected target nodes use a scanning TRACE LOCK reticle
Sparse one- and two-target layouts remain readable while synthetic infrastructure fills dead space
Quickhack execution dock remains intentionally clean so the network field carries the visual complexity
Retained all 0.8.4 hardening, 0.8.5 mask cleanup, and 0.8.6 execution controls
knownManualRules: Cyberdeck passive effects such as conditional RAM discounts are displayed but not automatically adjudicated because the installed FEHA module also treats them as descriptive/manual rules
Quickhack damage, saves, conditions, and chained effects are announced in chat but are not automatically applied; this matches the current installed FEHA Cyberdeck behavior

The exported world catalog contains legacy Quickhack description text whose written RAM values can disagree with flags.ramCost; V3 uses flags.ramCost as canonical and corrects its own display text without mutating source items
